evidence.quote: Taco Bell is introducing a month-long taco celebration of deals, drops and surprises featuring go-to menu orders from Kevin Hart, Paris Hilton and Doja Cat

To celebrate these launches, the Taco Bell Rewards program’s Tuesday Drop will include the chance to win one of 200 limited-edition Taco Bell x Flamin’ Hot puffer jackets on Nov. 17.

Overall the core facts are in the sources, but the Super Duolingo item being called a Tuesday Drop is a mild stretch. I judge it supported with this minor caveat.

crm_rows.title: Tuesday Drops and Rewards: pull in-person traffic into the app
crm_rows.what_happening: Taco Bell runs weekly app-only Tuesday Drops, including the $1 Kevin Hart's Usual, the 200 Flamin' Hot puffer jackets, the Pretty Pink Picnic Kit and a free month of Super Duolingo. Some rewards can be redeemed only in the app.
crm_rows.why_flowcode_fits: Drops are app-only, so every physical touchpoint (cups, bags, receipts, table tents, store windows) can drive members into the app. Taco Bell likely cannot tell which in-restaurant message brought someone into Rewards.
crm_rows.suggested_play: Your Tuesday Drops, from the $1 Kevin Hart's Usual in October to the 200 Flamin' Hot puffer jackets on Nov 17, are app-only. You likely cannot tell which in-restaurant or packaging message pulls guests in to join Rewards or enter a Drop. Put dynamic Flowcodes on cups, bags and in-store signage that open a FlowHub with the current Drop, an app download and a Rewards sign-up, changing each week without reprinting. You would get scans by store and market, app installs and new members by touchpoint, and a CRM sync. Flowcode's LOVE CORN packaging code produced a 62% CRM conversion. Which in-store touchpoint do you rely on today to drive Drop sign-ups?
crm_rows.would_measure: Scans by store and week, app installs, new Rewards members and Drop entries by touchpoint.

crm_rows.title: Live Más Open: turn the Peacock and Golf Channel broadcast into fan sign-ups
crm_rows.what_happening: Taco Bell produced the Live Más Open celebrity golf tournament with Kevin Hart in Laguna Beach on Nov 2. It streams on Peacock on Nov 20 and airs on Golf Channel. Experimental menu items were served at the event, and the winning team helps pick a discontinued item to return in 2027.
crm_rows.why_flowcode_fits: A broadcast and streaming show reaches many viewers, but there is likely no link from the screen to a Taco Bell Rewards sign-up or a vote. A QR code on screen gives a measurable response. The 2027 menu-return vote gives viewers a reason to act.
crm_rows.suggested_play: Your Live Más Open, streaming on Peacock Nov 20 and airing on Golf Channel, is a branded show with a built-in hook: the winning team helps pick which discontinued item returns in 2027. Today you likely cannot tell which viewers cared enough to act or who they are. Put a dynamic Flowcode on screen and in the show's graphics that opens a FlowHub where viewers vote on the item to bring back, join Taco Bell Rewards and download the app. You would get scans by airing and platform, new Rewards sign-ups and app installs tied to the show, and first-party data synced to your CRM. Flowcode's ESPN College GameDay broadcast code collected 32,000 emails in one day. How are you measuring the response to the show and tying viewers to the app today?
crm_rows.would_measure: Scans by airing and platform, vote participation, Rewards sign-ups, app installs and CRM-matched viewers.

crm_rows.title: Live Más LIVE variety show on Peacock
crm_rows.what_happening: Taco Bell's third annual Live Más LIVE, hosted by Vince Staples on March 10 in Hollywood, premiered on Peacock as a variety show and revealed over 20 menu items.
crm_rows.why_flowcode_fits: A national broadcast reveals menu items, but the link from viewing to trying an item or joining Rewards is likely invisible. An on-screen code can offer early access.
crm_rows.suggested_play: Your Live Más LIVE show, hosted by Vince Staples and streamed on Peacock after the March 10 Hollywood event, revealed more than 20 menu items to a national audience. You likely cannot see which viewers acted on them. Add a dynamic Flowcode during menu reveals that opens a FlowHub with early access signup and an app download, and update it as items launch. You would get scans per reveal and new members by item interest. Flowcode's Welch's campaign had a 55% click-through. How do you tie show viewers to menu trial today?
crm_rows.would_measure: Scans per reveal segment, early-access sign-ups, app installs and later item purchases.

crm_rows.title: Manager Mendoza campaign: link TV and the stadium store takeover to the Special
crm_rows.what_happening: Taco Bell's football-season campaign features franchise players Fernando Mendoza and Davante Adams. TV ads show Mendoza as a rookie store manager. A "Manager Mendoza's Special" meal deal ties in, along with a takeover of a real Taco Bell in a stadium.
crm_rows.why_flowcode_fits: The TV ads, the meal deal and the stadium store all point to one offer, but it is likely hard to see which touchpoint drives orders. A Flowcode on the spot and in the store can send people to the deal and the app with per-touchpoint tracking.
crm_rows.suggested_play: Your football-season campaign with Fernando Mendoza as a rookie store manager has been on TV since September, with a Manager Mendoza's Special and a stadium store takeover. You likely cannot see which of the TV spot, the stadium store or social drives people to the deal. Add a dynamic Flowcode to the TV spot and on in-store signage and cups at the stadium location, opening a FlowHub with the Special, an app download and a Rewards sign-up. You would get scans by touchpoint and market, app installs and new members attributed to each. Which touchpoint do you think is driving Special redemptions today, and how would you know?
crm_rows.would_measure: Scans per spot and per store, Special redemptions, app installs and Rewards sign-ups by touchpoint.

crm_rows.title: Decades Menu Vine campaign: connect the nostalgia spot to the merch drop
crm_rows.what_happening: Taco Bell launched a 2016-themed Decades Menu with a nostalgic spot built from Vines. It partnered with the Divine app and offered merch through a Rewards Tuesday Drop with Anti Social Social Club and Camp Snap.
crm_rows.why_flowcode_fits: The spot and the Divine partnership create interest, and the merch drop is a Rewards-only reward. A scannable link from the spot to the Drop can bring new viewers into Rewards and show which exposures led to sign-ups.
crm_rows.suggested_play: Your 2016-themed Decades Menu spot, launched in late August, comes with a Rewards Tuesday Drop of merch from Anti Social Social Club and Camp Snap. You likely cannot see how many people who watched the spot went on to join Rewards for the Drop. Put a dynamic Flowcode on the spot and a FlowURL in the Divine partnership content, opening a FlowHub with the Decades Menu, Drop access and a Rewards sign-up. You would get scans by channel, new Rewards members and Drop entries tied to each source. Flowcode's Lunchables campaign saw a 50% campaign conversion. How do you tell today which creative brings new members into the Tuesday Drop?
crm_rows.would_measure: Scans and clicks by creative and channel, new Rewards sign-ups, Drop entries and app installs.

crm_rows.title: Olivia Rodrigo pink Baja Blast and festival activation
crm_rows.what_happening: Taco Bell launched the Olivia Rodrigo pink Baja Blast, rolled out regionally then nationally on Sept 24, and ran a pink activation at her Daisy Chain Fields festival with samples and limited-edition merch.
crm_rows.why_flowcode_fits: Festival attendees get samples and merch but are likely not captured as known customers. A code on cups and merch can convert them into Rewards members.
crm_rows.suggested_play: Your pink Baja Blast activation at Olivia Rodrigo's Daisy Chain Fields festival gave out samples and limited-edition merch to a big young audience. You likely did not capture who they were or what they did next. Put a Flowcode on sample cups and merch that opens a FlowHub with Rewards sign-up, an app download and the nationwide drink availability. You would get scans by event, new members and later redemptions linked to the festival. Flowcode's CLEAR deployment saw 1.2M+ scans across 7,000+ codes. How do you follow up with festival guests today?
crm_rows.would_measure: Scans by event and item, Rewards sign-ups, app installs and follow-up redemptions.

crm_rows.title: Sauce packet recycling program with TerraCycle
crm_rows.what_happening: Taco Bell and TerraCycle run a US sauce packet recycling program, reporting one million items collected over five years.
crm_rows.why_flowcode_fits: Sauce packets can carry a code that opens recycling instructions and a Rewards sign-up, linking a sustainability message to measurable engagement.
crm_rows.suggested_play: Your TerraCycle sauce packet recycling program, reporting one million items collected over five years, relies on guests knowing about it. You likely cannot see how many learn of it from the packet. Add a Flowcode to sauce packets that opens a FlowHub with recycling instructions and a Rewards sign-up. You would get scans by product and region and sign-ups from sustainability-minded guests. How do you promote the program to guests today?
crm_rows.would_measure: Scans by packet type and region, program sign-ups, Rewards enrolment.

crm_rows.title: College Football Playoff tailgate Student Section
crm_rows.what_happening: Each year Taco Bell runs a Live Más Student Section for 500 students at the CFP National Championship Tailgate, with life-sized sauce packet photo ops and free food trucks, designed for TV and social exposure.
crm_rows.why_flowcode_fits: The activation gets broadcast and social visibility but likely captures little first-party data on the students. Codes at the photo ops and food trucks can turn presence into Rewards members.
crm_rows.suggested_play: Your yearly Live Más Student Section at the CFP National Championship Tailgate gives 500 students a stage-side experience, built for TV and social visibility. You likely cannot tell how many of those students became Rewards members. Put Flowcodes on the sauce packet photo ops, food truck windows and giveaways that open a FlowHub with Rewards sign-up and a share prompt. You would get scans by station, new members and emails from a young audience. What do you capture from tailgate guests after the event today?
crm_rows.would_measure: Scans by station, new Rewards sign-ups, emails captured and social shares.

crm_rows.title: College of Idaho basketball sponsorship
crm_rows.what_happening: Taco Bell sponsors College of Idaho basketball with its logo on women's team jerseys and the purple student section barriers.
crm_rows.why_flowcode_fits: Student section barriers are a visible spot for a code that converts students into Rewards members, with scans reported by game.
crm_rows.suggested_play: Your sponsorship of College of Idaho basketball, with the logo on jerseys and the purple student-section barriers since last season, reaches students at every home game. You likely have no way to measure sign-ups from it. Put a Flowcode on the barriers and arena screens opening a FlowHub with a Rewards sign-up and a game-day offer. You would get scans by game and new student members. Flowcode's NFL Shop code drove 10k connections in 60 seconds. How do you measure the return from your local sponsorships today?
crm_rows.would_measure: Scans by game, Rewards sign-ups, offer redemptions and nearby store traffic.
